Seminar Title:

COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF SUSTAINABLE PAVEMENT QUALITY CONCRETE INCORPORATING STEEL INDUSTRIES BY-PRODUCTS

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Civil Engineering

Speaker Name:

Priti Anurag Puri ( Rollno : 524ce1003)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, Civil Engineering Department

Date and Time:

02 Sep 2026 11:00 am

Contact:

Aditya Kumar Das

Abstract:

This research aims to design and evaluate a sustainable Pavement Quality Concrete (PQC) by incorporating industrial by-products such as aggregate replacements and binders in place of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC). The study focuses on utilising Linz-Donawitz (LD) slag and Induction Furnace (IF) slag as substitutes for conventional coarse and fine aggregates, respectively, along with Portland Slag Cement (PSC) as the primary binder. The experimental evaluations across fresh, mechanical, and durability properties demonstrated that all mix designs were in workable state of 25 &plusmn 10 mm, while at 90 days, the PSC mixes incorporating optimum replacement levels of industrial slag exhibited peak mechanical and durability performance. For LD slag as coarse aggregate at the 80% optimum replacement level in M40 grade PQC, the mix achieved a compressive strength of 58.52 MPa (compared to 55.56 MPa control), a flexural strength of 6.67 MPa and a slake durability index of 98.42% (compared to 97.88% control). Similarly, for IF slag as fine aggregate at the 60% optimum replacement level in M40 grade PQC, the mix reached a compressive strength of 55.11 MPa, flexural strength of 5.73 MPa (compared to 5.19 MPa control), and an improved slake durability index of 95.68%. consequently, the optimum replacement was identified as 80% LD slag for coarse aggregate and 60% IF slag for fine aggregate, both in M40 grade PQC, delivering superior strength and durability compared to control mixes. Optimisation was further carried out using the Taguchi L16 orthogonal array, and multi-response analysis through Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) identified the most balanced mix design. Future work will extend to fracture and deformation behaviour, fatigue performance under cyclic traffic loading, and integration of optimised results into Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA), ultimately leading to predictive models and guidelines for environmentally sustainable PQC suitable for large-scale field applications.
